nodes.description: Alkaline HER performance in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The IR-corrected polarization curves and Tafel plots are shown in Fig. 4a and b. ... the hybrid catalyst exhibits much enhanced alkaline HER activity with a low overpotential of 14 mV to drive 10 mA cm^{-2} and a Tafel slope of 33 mV dec^{-1}. In particular, the Ni_{0.2}Mo_{0.8}N/Ni hybrid catalyst delivers high current densities of 100 and 300 mA cm^{-2} at overpotentials of about 40 and 70 mV, respectively. ... A 60 h cycling test is conducted at 100 mA cm^{-2} ... After a period of 5000 CV cycle tests, the HER activity ... is maintained.

nodes.description: Alkaline HER performance in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The performance of Ni_{0.2}Mo_{0.8}N microrods is partly like Pt/C with low η_{10} of 61 mV, but the Tafel slope reaches 111 mV dec^{-1} indicating the rate determining step of the Volmer reaction.

nodes.description: Alkaline HER performance in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The porous Ni shows poor alkaline HER catalytic activity with η_{10} of 229 mV.

nodes.description: Alkaline HER performance in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The Pt/C (0.5 mg cm^{-2}) shows superior alkaline HER activity with a low overpotential of 10 mV to drive 10 mA cm^{-2} (η_{10}) and a Tafel slope of 51 mV dec^{-1} at the low polarization region. However, Pt/C exhibits unsatisfactory alkaline HER activity at high current density, which requires an overpotential of 124 mV and 206 mV to drive 100 mA cm^{-2} and 200 mA cm^{-2}, respectively.

nodes.description: Overall water splitting performance in 1 M KOH (NiFe LDH (+) || Ni0.2Mo0.8N/Ni (-))
nodes.source_text: a water-alkali electrolyzer is built up in a 1 M KOH solution using NiFe LDH as an anode and Ni_{0.2}Mo_{0.8}N/Ni as a cathode. ... The NiFe LDH^{(+)}//Ni_{0.2}Mo_{0.8}N/Ni^{(-)} coupled electrolyzer requires only a cell voltage of 1.52 V to achieve a water-splitting current density of 100 mA cm^{-2}, suggesting ~81% electrical-to-fuel efficiency. And this electrolyzer can maintain stability at high current densities up 200 mA cm^{-2}.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacings of 0.247 nm and 0.203 nm assigned to (100) plane of Ni0.2Mo0.8N and (111) plane of Ni, respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2e–g, the high-resolution TEM images demonstrate the well-resolved lattice fringes of the Ni0.2Mo0.8N/Ni microrod. The lattice spacings of 0.247 and 0.203 nm are assigned to the (100) and (111) planes of Ni0.2Mo0.8N and Ni, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of scratched Ni–Mo–N powder shows low crystallinity with peaks at 36.3° and 44.2° corresponding to (100) and (111) planes of hexagonal Ni0.2Mo0.8N and Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern of the scratched powder displays a low crystallinity and the peaks at 36.3° and 44.2° can be well associated with the (100) and (111) planes of hexagonal Ni0.2Mo0.8N (JCPDS No. 029-0931) and Ni (JCPDS No. 004-0850).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p shows metallic Ni peaks at 853.3 eV and 870.5 eV (Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/2), Ni2+ at 856.2 eV and 873.9 eV; Mo 3d shows Mo3+ at 229.8 eV and 232.9 eV, Mo4+ at 230.8 eV and 233.5 eV, Mo6+ at 232.5 eV and 235.9 eV; N 1s and Mo 3p at 395.6 eV (Mo 3p3/2), 397.8 eV (N–Mo/Ni), 399.5 eV (N–H).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As for the Ni0.2Mo0.8N/Ni, two peaks centered at 853.3 eV and 870.5 eV are observed in the Ni 2p spectrum, which correspond to the Ni 2p1/2 and Ni 2p3/2 of the metallic Ni phase... The N 1s and Mo 3p spectrum shows three peaks at 395.6 eV, 397.8 eV and 399.5 eV, corresponding to Mo 3p3/2, N–Mo/Ni and N–H bonds.
